teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Five billion dollars of AI chips, one storefront office. Meet Megaspeed, and its strange rise.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: the blue-eyed presenter in fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch stands on a dusk street facing a small, plain storefront office, medium shot, moody lighting, no text.

teile.name: Takeover
teile.text: In 2023, investors bought a Singapore gaming subsidiary and renamed it Megaspeed.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: anonymous illustrative investors shake hands with a manager in a modern Singapore office while workers swap a blank sign outside the window, medium shot, cool daylight, no likeness of real people.

teile.name: Chip access
teile.text: Alibaba became its anchor customer, and it became an Nvidia Cloud Partner.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: long rows of glowing server racks in a data centre, the fedora-wearing presenter walks the aisle inspecting equipment, wide shot, cool blue lighting, no logos.

teile.name: Scale
teile.text: Priority chip access followed. By November 2023, it had acquired around $5 billion in chips.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: workers wheel crates of server hardware through a bright loading bay toward a data centre, the presenter watching from the side, wide shot, crisp daylight, no text.

teile.name: Investigation
teile.text: So what changed? By 2024, U.S. authorities suspected those chips reached Chinese companies without permission.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: investigators in dark coats examine stacked shipping crates on a night-time container dock, flashlight beams cutting through haze, medium shot, tense low-key lighting, no text.

teile.name: Scrutiny widens
teile.text: Singapore and Malaysia investigated too. Its owner Swiftdata had just one storefront office.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: night view of Kuala Lumpur towers, the fedora presenter stands on a rooftop looking toward the city lights, over-the-shoulder shot, restrained blue and amber lighting.

teile.name: Ending
teile.text: Billions, one storefront. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Original painted open-world-game poster style: the blue-eyed presenter in fedora and grey suit checks his gold pocket watch in front of the same small storefront office at dusk, medium shot, warm reflective light, no text.

story.besserer_hook: Five billion dollars of AI chips hidden in one tiny storefront office.

hooklabor.alt: Five billion dollars of AI chips, one storefront office.
kandidaten: Megaspeed bought around five billion dollars of Nvidia chips in months.
An investor buys a sleepy Singapore gaming subsidiary and renames it Megaspeed.
Megaspeed became an Nvidia Cloud Partner almost overnight, and it was brutal.
Megaspeed's chips drew investigations in the U.S., Singapore and Malaysia.
Megaspeed ended up under investigation by three governments over Nvidia chips.

belege.name: Megaspeed
belege.text:
Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. is a cloud computing provider based in Singapore. It supplies artificial intelligence computing power and hosting services.
The company was founded in 2015 as 7Road International PTE, the Singaporean subsidiary of the Chinese gaming firm 7Road Holdings. It was acquired by Chinese investor Alice Huang in 2023, and renamed to Megaspeed. Huang served as the company's director from March to November 2023, when the company was acquired by Singaporean citizen Tan Yong Pong through his company Swiftdata. Reporting indicates Huang continue to exercise leadership over the company afterwards. Megaspeed established a close business partnership with the online Chinese retailer Alibaba Group, which became its biggest client and anchor customer for cloud services in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed also developed ties with Nvidia, becoming an Nvidia Cloud Partner. Megaspeed bought billions of dollars worth Nvidia products for data centres throughout Southeast Asia, including in Malaysia.
From 2024, the company came under investigation by the U.S. authorities for suspicions it was supplying Nvidia chips to Chinese companies without U.S. government permission. Singapore and Malaysia also launched their own investigations. The company came under further scrutiny following reports that Alice Huang was in a romantic relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.


History: Megaspeed was founded in 2015 as 7Road International PTE, the Singaporean subsidiary of the Chinese gaming firm 7Road Holdings. In 2023, a few months after the United States government imposed export restrictions on artificial intelligence chips to China, Chinese investor Alice Huang and a group of investors acquired the subsidiary. The purchase was done through a British Virgin Islands-registered company associated with Huang called Huang Le Ltd. After the purchase, the company was renamed to Megaspeed International in March 2023. Huang joined the company and serving as its managing director until November 2023. Huang also served as the director and managing director of the company's Indonesia subsidiary in the same period. Kang Wei, an executive at the private equity firm Shanghai Hexi, also worked with Huang in building the business. According to a human resources manager contacted by the The New York Times in 2025, most of Megaspeed's directors were based in China and rarely visited Singapore, while James Tan, the company's Singapore director, was never present.
In November 2023, Megaspeed was acquired from Huang Le Ltd by Swiftdata, a Singapore-based company owned by Singaporean citizen Tan Yong Pong, which had been incorporated a few weeks before. Following the acquisition, Tan became Megaspeed's sole director. As of October 2025, Tan was residing in Shanghai. According to an investigation by Culper Research, Huang was still in charge of the company in May 2026. The Journal also reported that she continued to act as the company's leader since then, introducing herself as Megaspeed's CEO to a business partner as recently as August 2025. On November 15, 2026, Megaspeed said Huang had left the company on August 30, 2025 and had no current rule there. Huang continued to participate in participate in the chip procurement and fundraising work of Swiftdata as a senior manager until she left the company in 2025. Swiftdata's actual office scale in Singapore was limited, with only one storefront office and only 2 to 10 employees listed on LinkedIn. Agence France-Presse reported that the contact number listed on the company's official website was actually a private residence. The New York Times reported Swiftdata's address led to an accounting firm in Singapore, where employees did not know how to reach Tan. In 2024, Megaspeed registered affiliates across the United States, Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand. In the same year, Tan established Speedmatrix, a Malaysia-based subsidiary. The New York Times reported that the registered address of Speedmatrix in shipping records was a "dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur, where the sign out front advertised a construction company". Speedmatrix has an office on the upper floors of a shopping mall in Johor.
One of Megaspeed's biggest clients became Alibaba Group, the online Chinese retailer. Megaspeed was Alibaba Group's anchor customer for cloud services in Southeast Asia since the beginning, and was its biggest client. The Wall Street Journal reported Alibaba Group was looking for a partner that would help it access data centers with chips from the American multinational technology corporation Nvidia. Megaspeed told the Nvidia team in an early meeting about its relationship with Alibaba Group. Megaspeed later told Nvidia that Alibaba Group would be an anchor customer. Later, Megaspeed became an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region, giving the company priority access to chips, and acquired around US$5 billion in AI chips and advanced hardware in November 2023. According to The Wall Street Journal, Alice Huang had leveraged her connections with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to get Megaspeed to become an Nvidia Cloud Partner. According to the Journal, Megaspeed also brought servers it acquired from Nvidia to data centers in Malaysia, which provided computing power to Alibaba, and shipped some of the servers to China, including the Shanghai-based Century Litong which Kang had done business with. In June 2024, Alibaba Group, through its Singaporean subsidiary called Apex Enterprise Solutions, lent money to Megaspeed, via its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix, with Speedmatrix pledging its entire business as collateral for the loan. In 2024, Megaspeed's balance sheet increased from $33 million to $3 billion, mostly due to its subsidiaries’ dealings. In the summer of 2024, Megaspeed International entered into a joint partnership with Nvidia. Megaspeed was planning on purchasing $2 billion of Nvidia's stock.
The Journal reported Kang and Huang planned several data centre projects from late 2024 to June 2025, including two in Southeast Asia and one in Shanghai, with the couple expressing confidence expecting to triple their money in three years and get Nvidia chips to China. Also, in 2024, Megaspeed investor presentation featured a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project, an artificial intelligence data center located in Shanghai. Between May and June 2024, a subsidiary of Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company founded by Alice Huang and majority-owned by her sister, Huang Yu, until January 2026, installed computing servers valued at ¥747 million renminbi at the Shanghai facility. Another company, Shanghai Shuoyao Technology Corporation, had installed Nvidia H100 and H200 processors on its data center. Shanghai Shuoyao has been described by Bloomberg News as "something of Megaspeed’s Chinese corporate twin".
